label: first copy-phase input (orig(0) fed back, recall_idx 1) in length-9 sequences
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, almost entirely at step t=L+1 (input = the first fed-back output orig(0), right after <DEL>, while outputting orig(1)) in length-9 sequences (98.7% of mass at L=9; a few at L=8 and at recall_idx 2). Never fires in the original or delimiter phases or for L<=7. Only ~2% of L=9 recall_idx=1 steps exceed threshold: which ones depends on token content. It is more likely when the first token is n or r (then l, d, f, o) and when g, 2, 0, w or b appear among the next original tokens (orig(1..3)). Adding those token conditions raises precision to ~0.3 but drops recall to ~0.25 (best dev F1 ~0.27), which looks like a soft linear threshold over token identities, not a clean rule. The structural predicate gets ~0.94 recall and mass recall at very low precision (0.02). Magnitudes are tiny (max 0.013) and the top-activating examples are mostly n/r-initial sequences with g or 2 early.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: recall_idx=1 & in_tok=n (+3.93), phase=2 & in_tok=r (+3.31), phase=2 & out_tok=2 (+2.00), to_go=6 (+1.99), orig3=g (+1.95), t=10 & in_tok=d (+1.83). Lower it: orig8=- (-2.44), orig2=1 (-1.94), out_tok=v (-1.91), next_out=- (-1.87).
